main_text.head: AD ORNATISSIMUM JUVENEM D. JOHANNEM IRENÆUM, SS. THEOL. STUDIOSUM PULPITA PUBLICA CONSCENSURUM, AMICUM AC FRATREM CHARISSIMUM.
main_text.p: Est dubium multis ecclesia quæ sit in orbe, Dum turbant populum dogmata pontificum. Idcirco multi misere sub mole laborant In tenebrisq; errant perdita sicut ovis.
Interea clarum, claro de lumine lumen Per verbum Domini Christus in orbe micat. Verba docent ejus, sit quænam ecclesia vera Demonstrans populo dulce salutis iter.
Hanc qui studet clare doctrinam reddere Doctor Ingenio Crocius, judicioq; gravis: Dum verbo Domini, tot cæca sophismata solvit Ac Christi cœrus [?] vera sigilla notat.
Hanc ut defendas tua te, Irenæ fidelis, Admonet hoc pietas officiumq; tuum. Et præeunte tibi docto Doctore, sophistas Ut vincas, mandat religionis amor.
Ergo tibi frater, Christus dignetur adesse [?] Pugnantiq; suam porrigat ipse manum. Tu vero confide Deo, Deus optimus ille Et studia & vitæ diriget ipse tuas.
Ut possis prodesse bonis, servireq; Christo Et post hanc vitam regna tenere poli.

page.notes: The drop cap E of "Est" is joined to the word. The poem's stanza breaks are not clearly visible on the scan; the verse is grouped in fours by sense, which is an editorial choice. Doubtful readings: "cœrus" (possibly cœtus) and "adesse" (the scan may read "ad esse"). The printed fleuron below the signature is an ornament, not text, and is not transcribed. The text is slightly blurred at the right margin.
